clue.text: Forecourt offering a French guide to Porte de l'Evolution

parts.note: the French for 'a' (masculine) is un
to guide is to lead

indicators.note: evolution is gradual change of form, so the letters before it are reshaped into a new order

explanation.surface: A French guidebook to some Parisian gate or exhibition offered for sale at a petrol station forecourt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Porte de l'Evolution' looks like a real Paris landmark, but 'Evolution' is the signal to rework the first eight letters into the second word's ending.
explanation.definitionFit: Lead-free fuel is the standard product sold at a filling station's pumps, on its forecourt.

clue.text: Fruit cocktail

definitions.meaning: a crisp variety of eating apple sold under this name
a gin and grenadine drink with egg white, coloured rosy

explanation.surface: A fruit cocktail, as served at a party.
explanation.definitionFit: The name covers both a popular apple variety and a classic gin-based mixed drink.

clue.text: Some other pestilence

indicators.note: only some of the letters of the following words are taken, a run lying inside them

explanation.surface: Part of some other plague or epidemic.
explanation.definitionFit: A contagious viral infection loosely counts as a pestilence, a spreading disease.

clue.text: Unions here have another go at capturing soldiers position

indicators.note: capturing means the first word holds the soldiers inside it

parts.note: to have another go is to retry
GIs are American soldiers
a position or post can be an office

explanation.surface: Trade unions planning another attempt to seize a military post.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unions' looks like trade unions but means marriages, which in Britain may be conducted at a civil register venue rather than a church.
explanation.definitionFit: Civil marriages, unions, are held at the local register building, so this is the place where they take place.

clue.text: Attractive person on a poster, primarily exposed in a state of undress

parts.note: a dish is slang for a good-looking person
a bill is a printed notice or poster

indicators.note: primarily means only the opening letter of the next word is used

explanation.surface: A pin-up on a poster, shown semi-naked.
explanation.walkthrough: In this down clue 'on' places DISH above A BILL.
explanation.definitionFit: Borrowed from French, the word means being partly or casually clothed, a state of undress.

clue.text: Frog once found pincer movement by crab's head pernicious

indicators.note: movement says the letters of the word before shift about into a new order
a head is the top or start, so only the first letter of the word is taken

parts.note: something pernicious is harmful, harming

explanation.surface: A frog once witnessed a crab's claw manoeuvre that proved deadly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'movement' turns PINCER into PRINCE; C is the crab's head. In the fairy tale the frog was a prince under a spell.
explanation.definitionFit: In the fairy tale the enchanted frog turns back into the handsome royal hero when kissed.

clue.text: Rein charge that's getting circuitous

indicators.note: the clue word Rein is split so 'in' says the first part goes inside the charge

parts.note: to charge someone with a crime is to indict them
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: Pulling the reins in a way that leads round in circles.
explanation.walkthrough: The single word 'Rein' must be split as 'Re in', so it supplies both a piece and the containment signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Something circuitous goes the roundabout way, not straight to its target.

clue.text: Draw round receptacle for pipes

indicators.note: round means the first word goes around the second

parts.note: to draw or pull is to tug
a bin is a container or receptacle

explanation.surface: Sketch around a container meant for plumbing pipes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Draw' suggests sketching but means pull.
explanation.definitionFit: Lengths of hollow cylinder used to carry fluids are pipes, collectively.

clue.text: Product of an evil regime?

indicators.note: evil here signals the letters of the following word go badly wrong, into a corrupt new order

explanation.surface: What does a wicked dictatorship produce?
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition: someone forced into exile is what a bad regime produces.
explanation.definitionFit: Political exiles who have fled oppressive governments are a typical result of a tyrannical state.

clue.text: Elks frolicking in humid light

indicators.note: in means the reshuffled letters sit inside the other word

parts.note: humid air is damp

indicators.note: animals frolicking leap around, so these letters jump into a new order

explanation.surface: Elk playing about in a muggy climate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'light' looks like it describes the humid air but is the definition; 'frolicking' gives ESKL.
explanation.definitionFit: An angled lamp for a work surface is a kind of light.

clue.text: Local peaceful end is nigh, perhaps, as a perishing alternative

parts.note: a local is one's neighbourhood pub

indicators.note: the end of the word means only its last letter
perhaps signals the words could be arranged otherwise

explanation.surface: Things are quiet at the local, though the end of everything may be near.
explanation.walkthrough: Academics are told 'publish or perish', so the definition is the alternative to perishing. A pub is a British 'local'.
explanation.definitionFit: The academic maxim 'publish or perish' makes getting work into print the only other option to failure.

clue.text: He would have said no need for plastic surgery

definitions.text: He would have said no need for plastic surgery

indicators.note: surgery that reshapes features, so it reshapes these letters into another form

explanation.surface: A man so handsome he would refuse cosmetic surgery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plastic surgery' reshapes SAID NO; the whole clue describes the beautiful youth of Greek myth.
explanation.definitionFit: The youth loved by Aphrodite is the byword for male beauty, so he needs no cosmetic improvement.

clue.text: Rubbish pile with bronze award

indicators.note: rubbish as a verb means to trash, so these letters are knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: A heap of junk alongside a third-place medal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rubbish' looks like a noun beside 'pile' but signals the letters of PILE and BRONZE are mixed together.
explanation.definitionFit: The Stockholm and Oslo honours for science, literature and peace are a famous award.

clue.text: Celebrities may be the reason for TV dinners

definitions.text: may be the reason for TV dinners
definitions.meaning: having nowhere to sit and eat is why people eat off their laps in front of the television

explanation.surface: Famous people may be why we eat in front of the telly.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as NO TABLES, the second part describes a home without dining furniture.
explanation.definitionFit: Notable people are those worth noting: celebrities and dignitaries.

clue.text: Young lady put away discussion

parts.note: a deb, short for debutante, is a young lady entering society
to put away food is to eat it, so ate

explanation.surface: A girl tidied away a conversation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put away' means consumed, not stored.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal argument between opposing sides is a discussion.

clue.text: Fastest at which rise of the Mariana Trench?

indicators.note: in a down clue a rise reads the word upwards, so backwards

parts.note: the deepest point in the world's oceans, a deep spot

explanation.surface: How fast would the Mariana Trench rise?
explanation.walkthrough: The Mariana Trench is the ocean's deepest spot; 'rise of' turns DEEPSPOT upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Maximum velocity is the rate at which something goes fastest.

clue.text: County council Islamic extremists following a regular pattern

parts.note: Cy is a dictionary abbreviation for county
Cl is an abbreviation for council

indicators.note: extremists here are the outermost letters of the word

explanation.surface: A county council and Islamic radicals, as a news headline.
explanation.definitionFit: Something recurring in cycles repeats in a regular pattern.

clue.text: See 6
Broadway not as bad as the proverbial

indicators.note: bad signals the remaining letters are put in a wrong order
not says some letters are left out of the word

parts.note: read as A's, two letters A

explanation.surface: A Broadway show that wasn't as poor as people say.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not as' means without the A's: remove both A's from BROADWAY, then 'bad' rearranges BRODWY.
explanation.definitionFit: A person or thing that is proverbial for something is a byword for it.

clue.text: Fits a little over three in sleepy disposition

indicators.note: in puts the number inside the rearranged letters
disposition is arrangement, so the word's letters are disposed afresh

parts.note: pi is about 3.14, a little more than three

explanation.surface: Bouts of activity slightly more than thrice in a drowsy temperament.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disposition' rearranges SLEEPY into ELEPSY, which is opened after its E.
explanation.definitionFit: The neurological condition causes seizures, which are often called fits.

clue.text: See 1
Some streets are just the ticket for 9

definitions.meaning: streets with traffic allowed in a single direction only
an exile needs a single, not return, ticket

explanation.surface: Certain streets suit an exile perfectly.
explanation.walkthrough: '9' is the exile of 9 across, who will not be coming back.
explanation.definitionFit: Single-direction traffic streets and single tickets with no return share this term.

clue.text: See 4
Rooftops Mr Turner built to withstand the elements

indicators.note: a turner is one who turns, so the letters before it are turned around; also the painter J.M.W. Turner

explanation.surface: J.M.W. Turner painting rooftops designed to brave the weather.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mr Turner' looks like the painter (and the film about him); 'Turner' alone is the rearranging signal on ROOFTOPS MR.
explanation.definitionFit: Proof against storms means constructed to resist wind and rain, the elements.

clue.text: See 10
See 2
Ignore puzzles set centrally as a dispenser of 21

indicators.note: centrally means the inner letters of each word are taken

explanation.surface: Puzzles laid out in the middle are to be disregarded.
explanation.walkthrough: The middles are NO, ZZL and E; 21 is petrol, from 21 down.
explanation.definitionFit: The spout on a fuel pump hose dispenses the liquid into the tank.

clue.text: Immoral and indecent commercial

indicators.note: the clue word indecent is split, so 'in' puts the advert inside

parts.note: taken as written
an ad is a television commercial

explanation.surface: A lewd and offensive advert.
explanation.walkthrough: The single word 'indecent' must be split as 'in decent', giving the containment signal and the outer word.
explanation.definitionFit: Self-indulgent and morally degenerate behaviour is immoral.
